clue.text: Like the page appearing in jewellery, it's grating

indicators.note: the pair of pieces shows up inside the word for jewellery, so one is placed within the other

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
like means as
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A page tucked inside jewellery makes an irritating scratching noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' puts AS and P inside RING, splitting it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasping voice or sound is harsh and scraping, which is what grating means.

clue.text: Remember the City in press, broadcast etc

indicators.note: the City's abbreviation goes inside the word for press

parts.note: to roll is to press flat, as with a rolling pin
EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: Recall the City's coverage in newspapers, broadcasting and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets EC inside ROLL after the R; 'broadcast' turns ETC into ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to bring back to mind, to recall.

clue.text: Wrap up well in headscarf and move in ungainly fashion

parts.note: read as head of scarf, its first letter S
to waddle is to walk clumsily, rocking side to side

explanation.surface: Bundle up warmly in a headscarf and shuffle awkwardly along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headscarf' must be split as head + scarf: the head of the word scarf is S.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle is to wind cloth snugly round a baby, so to bundle it up warmly.

clue.text: The supervisor crept in so cunningly

indicators.note: cunningly means craftily, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The boss sneaked in slyly to catch the workers out.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who oversees and checks others' work.

clue.text: Road metal — or is mettle?

definitions.meaning: small broken stones spread on roads

explanation.surface: Is the stuff for roads the same as spirit?
explanation.walkthrough: Road metal is British for the crushed stone used in road-making; 'mettle' plays on it sounding like metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravelly chips spread on icy roads, and also pluck or staying power.

clue.text: Left by accident in the church

indicators.note: by means next to, so the letter for left sits beside the word for accident

parts.note: chance is an accident or fluke

explanation.surface: Something was left behind by accident in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, so it stands for the church by naming a part of it.

clue.text: Able to admit opposing a particular design of bridge

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the word for able takes the other piece inside

parts.note: clever means able or skilful
anti means opposing or against

explanation.surface: Capable of accepting objections to a certain type of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' puts ANTI inside CLEVER after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever bridge is built from arms projecting from piers and supported at one end only.

clue.text: Passage in which the French support very good point

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so the French article comes last

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
S is a compass point, south
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A corridor where French people prop up an excellent point.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-class, appears as AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a gangway or walkway between rows of seats or pews.

clue.text: A buccaneer's rude-sounding shanty

indicators.note: sounding signals that the word for rude is said aloud, giving letters that are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: coarse means rude or vulgar
a shanty is a sailors' song, and an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A pirate's sea song sounds rather vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE said aloud gives CORS, before AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate, especially one of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Superior port

definitions.meaning: a feudal lord to whom vassals owed service
a Belgian city on the Meuse with a large inland river harbour

explanation.surface: A higher-ranking harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal overlord, and also the Belgian city on the Meuse with a major river harbour.

clue.text: Cold girl, but kind

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl may seem cold yet be kind at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a kind or category of things.

clue.text: Island Hotel — one's quite unrestricted here

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
one is I and 's stands for is, giving I then S
free means entirely without restriction

explanation.surface: An island hotel where guests are at complete liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Innisfree is the lake isle in Lough Gill, Ireland, made famous by W. B. Yeats's poem 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Innisfree is a small isle in Lough Gill, County Sligo, celebrated by Yeats.

clue.text: A youngster took the initiative and served out the soup

parts.note: a lad is a youngster
led means took the lead or showed initiative

explanation.surface: A boy took charge and dished up the soup.
explanation.definitionFit: To ladle is to serve liquid with a deep long-handled spoon, so the past tense means dished out the soup.

clue.text: Current needed to time contest?

parts.note: tide is an old word for time or season, as in Yuletide
a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: Is a current required to time a race?
explanation.walkthrough: TIDE as time survives in Eastertide and 'time and tide'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide-race is a fast tidal current in a narrow channel of the sea.

clue.text: Seafood as the principal part of a meal?

definitions.text: Seafood as the principal part of a meal?

parts.words: Seafood as the principal part of a meal?
parts.note: the main is the sea in poetry, so a dish from the main suggests fish served as the central dish of dinner

explanation.surface: Fish being served as the centrepiece of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The central and most substantial dish of a dinner, after starters and before dessert.

clue.text: Not at all inclined to stand up

definitions.meaning: vertical, with no lean or slope whatever
set up straight, as one raises a tent or a monument

explanation.surface: Someone with no wish whatever to get to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at all inclined' reads as unwilling, but it means not sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright with no slant at all, and also the verb for raising or setting up a structure.

clue.text: Though this may be true, spare the cracks!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words may be rearranged into the answer, so this signals a reshuffle

explanation.surface: Even if the claim is correct, spare us the jokes or gaps!
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' shuffles TRUE plus SPARE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertures are openings or gaps, such as cracks in a surface.

clue.text: Like an orange? One from N. Africa?

definitions.meaning: of a deep orange-red colour, or a small citrus fruit
a native of Tangier in Morocco

explanation.surface: Is this orange-like thing from North Africa?
explanation.definitionFit: A colour or fruit resembling an orange, and also a person from the Moroccan port of Tangier.

clue.text: Certain to be without a cleaner — note extra money needed!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for certain goes round the rest

parts.note: sure means certain
a char is a cleaning woman, a charlady
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: We're sure to be left without a cleaner, and extra cash is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: SURE wraps CHARG, which sits between R and E. A CHAR is British for a hired cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added on top of the usual price.

clue.text: To make cuts without hesitation shows a democratic spirit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cutting word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: to lance is to cut into, as a surgeon lances a boil
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Cutting things without pausing shows a fair-minded attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: LANCE wraps round ER, giving LERANCE after TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting views different from one's own is the open-minded spirit of a democracy.

clue.text: Member going around Ireland having a sly look

indicators.note: the limb word goes round the poetic name for Ireland

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A limb circles Ireland while giving a sidelong glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' puts ERIN inside LEG after LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leering means looking at someone in a sly, knowing or lustful way.

clue.text: He'll call about a fellow's retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the pair of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone will phone regarding a colleague's retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns REMAN round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who names a thing is one who calls it something.

clue.text: People retain a right to travel — battle for it

indicators.note: the word for people keeps the two letters held inside it

parts.note: men means people
go means to travel or move

explanation.surface: People keep the right to go on a journey and fight for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retain' puts A and R inside MEN after the M. Marengo was Napoleon's 1800 victory in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Marengo is a battle fought in 1800 in Piedmont, where Napoleon defeated the Austrians.

clue.text: A worker well used to being whistled at!

definitions.text: A worker well used to being whistled at!

parts.words: A worker well used to being whistled at!
parts.note: suggests a wolf-whistled person, but means a farm animal that works to the shepherd's whistle

explanation.surface: Someone at work who is quite used to builders' wolf whistles.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie on a farm works sheep, steered by its handler's whistle commands.

clue.text: Be silent and colour just a little

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Keep quiet and paint only a touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap, as in not a shred of evidence.

clue.text: Place to find a young boy represented in stone

definitions.text: a young boy represented in stone

parts.note: to put is to place
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spot where you can find a little boy carved in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a figure of a chubby child, often winged, in Renaissance art and sculpture.

clue.text: There'll be insufficient if many land

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword convention for many
earth means land or ground

explanation.surface: If there are too many people for the land, supplies will run short.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, a situation where there is not enough of something.

clue.text: Inch border

explanation.surface: A small measure at the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep forward bit by bit, and also the outer rim or margin of something.

clue.text: Bragged of rise to assembly when in the red

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed within the word for the colour

parts.note: taken as written, the colour red

indicators.note: assembly means putting the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Boasting of a rise to parliament while one's finances were overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' shuffles RISE TO into OISTER; 'in' puts it inside RED, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily and swagger, so the past tense covers boasting and showing off.

clue.text: Not all of the spinners will be on target

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, so the answer lies hidden inside it

explanation.surface: Some of the spin bowlers will hit the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, spinners are slow bowlers who make the ball turn.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the inner is the ring just outside the bull, so a hit there is close to the mark.

clue.text: Follow with spray for a flowering shrub

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
the rose is the sprinkler head on a watering can

explanation.surface: Trail along with a spray to treat a flowering bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild climbing rose of hedgerows with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Where the viewer's always seated

parts.note: suggests a cinema or television seat, but the viewer is the organ of sight sitting in its socket

explanation.surface: The spot where a television watcher is permanently installed.
explanation.definitionFit: The orbit or socket of the skull is where each organ of sight sits.
